artists.biography:
Echobelly were a Britpop band, debuting in 1994 with their album Everyone's Got One. They were often compared to Blondie and were influenced by Morrissey, who himself was a fan of the group.
The most prominent part of Echobelly's success formula was vocalist Sonya Madan, who was also the group's primary lyricist. Born in Delhi, India, before moving to England at the age of two, Madan had an unusual background for a pop star. Her rigid upbringing made rock music taboo for her as a youngster, and she did not attend her first rock concert until she was in college. In 1990 she met Glenn Johansson, a guitarist from Sweden who was pursuing a career in music. Johansson had previously edited a Swedish pornographic magazine called Eros, which may have contributed to the band's focus on sexual issues in many of their songs. He and Madan dated for a while, then remained friends after breaking up.

perplexity.description:
On, released in 1995, is the second album by British rock band Echobelly, following their 1994 debut Everyone's Got One. The album was recorded at Konk Studios in London and mixed at Fort Apache Studio in Boston, with producers Sean Slade and Paul Kolderie, known for their skill in capturing guitar sounds. Musically, On blends sharp, melodic rock with elements appealing to both Britpop and shoegaze audiences, featuring confident and honest lyrics by lead singer Sonya Aurora Madan and guitarist Glenn Johansson. The album is noted for its strong melodies and a more defined edge compared to their debut, positioning it as a significant work within the mid-90s Britpop movement.

Commercially, On was successful, reaching number 4 on the UK charts, supported by singles like "Great Things," which peaked at number 8. The album's release was accompanied by sold-out tours, enhancing Echobelly's rising profile in the British music scene. Critically, On is regarded as one of the standout albums of the Britpop era, praised for its blend of euphoria and sharp rock sensibility without veering into prog or other genres. It solidified Echobelly's place in the 1990s UK rock landscape and remains a key part of their discography.
